# Taxonomy resolution ladder  (grain)

For questions like _Is there a decoupling in taxonomy and functional trends across taxonomic levels?_, we need to evaluate if taxonomic and functional trends are consistent across different taxonomic levels/resolution/grain-levels. The goal is to determine how the taxonomy curve maps against the KO
function reference.
When we select a taxonomic resolution that is "cherry-picked", we run the risk of have a less appropriate output. If the story changes when we change the taxonomic level, that can be alarming and not responsible. Ramond et al. (2025) looked at how decoupling is only credible if it survives across grain, not at one cherry-picked resolution.

# Set up

```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
source(if (file.exists("_setup.R")) "_setup.R" else "scripts/_setup.R")
long <- load_long_annot()
```

## Build paired df

Shared prep for 03–06 (`R/prep_paired.R`): Gorda Ridge, Von Damm and Piccard; no per-row TPM cutoff; multi-KO transcripts split with TPM divided equally; Eukaryota-only and Opisthokonta lineages dropped. `depth = NULL` because the ladder assigns its own depth at each step.

```{r paired-table}
paired <- prep_paired(long, depth = NULL)
# head(paired)
meta <- paired |>
  distinct(sample_id, sample_unit, field, vent_bin, n_reps) |>
  arrange(sample_id)

# length((long$SEQ_ID)); length((paired$SEQ_ID))
length(unique(long$SEQ_ID)); length(unique(paired$SEQ_ID))
```


## Set up the grain ladder 

Write a function to go through each taxonomic level. 

```{r ladder-setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# Same transcripts at every depth: keep rows with a resolvable lineage, rm NAs
paired_lin <- paired |> 
  filter(!is.na(full_classification))

# Grain ladder runs on the curated taxonomy (02 manual curation; 2026-10-12)
# depth 2 = curated supergroup, 3 = curated phylum (Syndiniales split from
# Dinophyta), 4 = class-level taxon inside its curated phylum, 5+ = deeper real
# ranks. See R/taxonomy_curated.R.
cur_key <- paired_lin |>
  distinct(full_classification, SUPERGROUP_0, SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM)
tax_at_depth <- function(d) {
  cur_key |>
    mutate(.tax = curated_lineage(full_classification, SUPERGROUP_0, SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM, d)) |>
    select(full_classification, .tax)
}

# deepest curated depth present
max_depth <- max(stringr::str_count(tax_at_depth(99L)$.tax, ";") + 1L)
# max_depth
```


```{r grain-fit-fn}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# dat - input taxonomy matrix
# feat - input functional matrix
# label - add a label for matrix used
# Label grain - for the taxonomic level used. 
grain_fit <- function(dat, feat, label_matrix, label_grain) {
  tryCatch( # stop if error
    { # Build matrix for adonis2 fxn to run.
    bm <- build_matrix(dat, feat, min_tpm = 0, transform = params$transform)
    m  <- meta[match(labels(bm$dist), meta$sample_id), ]
    # PERMANOVA function
    perm <- run_permanova(bm$dist, m,
                          permutations = params$permutations,
                          seed = params$seed) |>
      filter(.data$term %in% c("vent_bin", "field")) |>
      select(term, R2, p)
    # dispersion check following permanova
    disp <- c(vent_bin = betadisper_check(bm$dist, m$vent_bin)$dispersion_p,
              field    = betadisper_check(bm$dist, m$field)$dispersion_p)
    #
    perm |> mutate(matrix = label_matrix, 
                   grain = label_grain,
                   n_features = ncol(bm$mat), 
                   dispersion_p = disp[.data$term],
                   skip_reason = NA_character_,
                   .before = 1)}, 
    error = function(e) {
    # if fails, stop.
    message(label_matrix, " grain ", 
            label_grain, " skipped: ", 
            conditionMessage(e))
    tibble::tibble(matrix = label_matrix, 
                   grain = label_grain, term = NA_character_,
                   R2 = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, 
                   n_features = NA_integer_,
                   dispersion_p = NA_real_, 
                   skip_reason = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}
```

```{r ladder-check}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
glimpse(paired_lin) # paired rows with a lineage (same as paired)
glimpse(max_depth) # Determined ceiling for taxonomic grain.
```

Start with taxonomy "2". taxa level 1 was only "Eukaryota" so it would have thrown an error. Note that these checks across taxonomic lienages also need to be run with all functional counts and then all with prevalence filtered data.
```{r ladder-run}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# unfiltered and prevalence-filtered
## Across the different levels, 2 to the max_depth, run this function. Where we do a grain fit 
tax_curve <- purrr::map_dfr(2:max_depth, function(d) {
  dd <- paired_lin |> dplyr::left_join(tax_at_depth(d), by = "full_classification")
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    grain_fit(dd,".tax", "taxonomy", d),
    grain_fit(prevalence_filter(dd, ".tax", 4), ".tax", "taxonomy_prev", d)
  )
})

# KO function reference (same two filters), horizontal line on the plot
fxn_curve <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  grain_fit(paired_lin, "ko_id", "function", NA_integer_),
  grain_fit(prevalence_filter(paired_lin, "ko_id", 4), "ko_id", "function_prev", NA_integer_)
)
# _prev will be added to the prevalence filtered matrices.
```

```{r ladder-peek}
head(tax_curve)
head(fxn_curve) # Grain is NA, just the 4 options. 
```

View results.
```{r ladder-table}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
grain_curve <- dplyr::bind_rows(tax_curve, fxn_curve)
readr::write_csv(grain_curve, "output-tables/03_grain_curve.csv")
grain_curve |> dplyr::arrange(term, matrix, grain)
```

## Annotation resolution by grain

Fraction of expression (scaledTPM) whose deepest retained rank is a real taxon name rather than a placeholder. Using TPM, not distance matrices, so it is independent of the rclr/distance choice. 

```{r resolution-by-depth}
# RM taxa with these:
placeholder <- "Indeterminate|Unannotated|incertae|_X$|^SG_|^Eukaryote$"

resolution_by_depth <- paired_lin |>
  dplyr::mutate(n_real = stringr::str_count(lineage_depth(full_classification, 99L), ";") + 1L) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(grain = 2:max_depth) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    resolved_frac_tpm = sum(scaledTPM[n_real >= grain], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(scaledTPM),
    .by = grain) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    purrr::map_dfr(2:max_depth, \(d) tibble::tibble(
      grain = d,
      n_features = dplyr::n_distinct(tax_at_depth(d)$.tax))),
    by = "grain")

resolution_by_depth

readr::write_csv(resolution_by_depth, "output-tables/03_resolution_by_depth.csv")
```

### Supp figure S2
```{r grain-plot}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 13
ref <- fxn_curve |> dplyr::select(term, matrix, R2)   # KO reference lines

pal <- c(taxonomy = "#5a82b3", taxonomy_prev = "#34454c",
         `function` = "#eeb480", function_prev = "#c16b27")

p_grain_r2 <- ggplot(tax_curve, aes(grain, R2, color = matrix)) +
  geom_hline(data = ref, aes(yintercept = R2, color = matrix), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = p < 0.05, fill = dispersion_p >= 0.05), size = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 21, `FALSE` = 24),
                     name = "PERMANOVA p < 0.05") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "white"),
                    name = "Dispersion homogeneous\n(PERMDISP p >= 0.05)") +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal, name = NULL) + # USed Wada random 4-color
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:max_depth) +
  facet_wrap(~ term) +
  labs(x = "taxonomic depth (ranks kept)",
       y = expression(R^2~"(marginal)")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        strip.background = element_blank())
```


```{r grain-plot-3}
# Plot the share of scaledTPM that resolves for each taxonomic depth.
frac_at <- function(g) {
  v <- resolution_by_depth$resolved_frac_tpm[resolution_by_depth$grain == g]
  if (length(v) == 1) round(100 * v) else NA_integer_
}

p_grain_tpm <- ggplot(resolution_by_depth, aes(grain, resolved_frac_tpm)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#34454c", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(resolved_frac_tpm, accuracy = 1)),
            vjust = -0.6, size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(aes(y = 0, label = paste0(n_features, " taxa")),
            vjust = 1.8, size = 2.7, colour = "grey35") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#34454c", `FALSE` = "grey82"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:max_depth) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, 1.14), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "taxonomic depth (ranks kept)",
       y = "scaledTPM classified to this depth") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 14, 5.5))
```


```{r grain-plot-panel}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 13
(p_grain_r2 | p_grain_tpm) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Taxonomic grain: the answer is flat across grain, the coverage is not",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Left: marginal R\u00b2 per term. Dashed = KO function reference; ",
      "circles = PERMANOVA p < 0.05, triangles = n.s.; filled = homogeneous dispersion.\n",
      "Right: share of scaledTPM resolving to each depth (taxon count below each bar); ",
      "rank 4 highlighted."))

# ggsave("figures/tax-level-study-supp.svg", width = 13, height = 5, device = "svg", limitsize = FALSE)
```

Circles = PERMANOVA p < 0.05; triangles = n.s. Filled = homogeneous dispersion (PERMDISP p >= 0.05), so R² reads as a composition difference; open = groups also differ in spread (Anderson & Walsh 2013).
